SCOUT_EVIDENCE_UPDATE/v1 — 2026-09-16

status: EVIDENCE_STRENGTHENED / NOT EXECUTION-AUTHORIZED

New primary research evidence relevant to this candidate: **Agent Zero Memory: Provenance-Aware Long-Term Memory for LLM Agents** (Wu & Zhu, arXiv:2608.29606, 2026-08-30), https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.29606

Reported architecture uses three parallel provenanced memory views (episodic events, entity-event graph, citation-locked hierarchical documentary memory), an intent gate that avoids memory work for self-contained turns, source routing, and concurrent hybrid retrieval. The paper reports 95.60% LongMemEval and 93.60% LoCoMo, and—more decision-relevant for #224—an eight-backbone study where accuracy varied only 3.4 points while per-query cost varied ~30x, with near-SOTA quality at up to ~20x lower cost. Treat all benchmark figures as author-reported until independently reproduced.

Decision implication: this strengthens the hypothesis behind #224 that **memory/retrieval architecture can dominate model-size/model-cost choice**. The cheapest next falsification remains unchanged: measure how often a deterministic zero-model reflex + exact/graph lookup can avoid semantic/LLM retrieval without harming recall. No reason yet to adopt Agent Zero Memory wholesale or allocate scarce Codex.

Additional design hint: preserve provenance/timestamp/evidence pointer on every learned item and enforce citation-lock/abstention semantics in any future memory benchmark. This is compatible with the existing candidate and does not justify a new duplicate Issue.

Quota discipline: web/Git research only; no downstream Work/Codex/local runner invoked; missing quota counters not estimated.
